items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline ('Demoted... and smaller than a country', 'Small comfort', 'still Russian'). Sound genuinely surprised on 'Pluto beats Russia'. Keep a steady, lively pace.
lines: You think Russia is bigger than Pluto?
Most books agreed with you... Until twenty fifteen.
Russia is huge. Seventeen point one million square kilometres. Eleven time zones.
And Pluto? Through Hubble, just a blurry dot... about twenty-three hundred kilometres wide.
Do the maths: Pluto's whole surface, about sixteen point six million. Russia wins.
Then in two thousand six, it got worse for Pluto.
Astronomers voted it out of the planet club. Demoted... and smaller than a country.
So how do you measure a world nobody has seen up close?
You go there. NASA's New Horizons flew for nine and a half years... nearly five billion kilometres.
July, twenty fifteen. It finally measured Pluto: twenty-three seventy-seven kilometres wide.
Bigger than the guess. So its surface? About seventeen point seven million.
Pluto beats Russia... by about six hundred and fifty thousand square kilometres. Almost a whole Texas.
Russia still has eleven time zones, though... Small comfort.
Russia never shrank. We just... finally looked.
And the twist? Half of Pluto's famous heart... has a Russian name.
Sputnik Plan-ISH-ee-uh. Named after Earth's first satellite, launched by the Soviet Union.
So, on paper... a little piece of Pluto is still Russian.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
